html:
An edict of 1588 in which Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who had just united Japan, ordered farmers across the country to hand over their swords, spears, bows and guns. The order said the metal would be used for nails in a great Buddha statue he was building in Kyoto.

During the Warring States century, farmers had often fought, and peasant leagues and armed temple communities had defied lords. Hideyoshi himself was the son of a foot soldier who had risen to rule. Taking away weapons was meant to stop anyone else from doing the same.

Together with his land survey and an order of 1591 that kept warriors and farmers in separate classes, the hunt drew a hard line between samurai, who bore arms and lived in castle towns, and peasants, who farmed and paid tax. The Tokugawa shoguns kept this order for over two centuries, until the Meiji government abolished the samurai class.
